headline: The US drug regulator has warned a software maker that releasing a new AI algorithm and moving its product to the web required fresh FDA clearance.
score_reason: Concrete regulatory signal for AI medical software, but one company's letter, read through a law firm's summary.
importance_line: Makers of AI medical software, and the clinicians and patients who rely on their updates, are affected, but this is a single warning letter and Orrick's view that scrutiny will continue is a forecast.
summary: Law firm Orrick reports that the FDA's device centre sent a warning letter to O.N. Diagnostics, saying version 3.0.0 of its spine-scan fracture software (VirtuOst VFA) went beyond its earlier clearance because it added a new algorithm and moved the product to the web without a new 510(k), the FDA's pre-market notice for devices. The FDA asked the company to stop distributing that version; Orrick advises makers of software as a medical device that even routine releases can be regulatory events.
notes: The FDA letter itself was not read. A 510(k) is the premarket notification a maker files to show a device is similar to one already cleared. Date of the letter not stated; Orrick alert is dated Oct 2026 and was published 9 Oct.
